A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SnapMoGen dataset and MoMask++ method. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation experiments on HumanML3D and SnapMoGen, component ablations, reconstruction analyses, and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a caption-augmentation ablation and an analysis of token completion during inference.

M1.justification: The shared-codebook multi-scale quantizer, single masked transformer, training losses, text-conditioning alternatives, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The added experiments examine existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions use HumanML3D and SnapMoGen with the same motion and task coverage, including the same casual-prompt examples. The added ablation and decoding analysis do not establish a new dataset, population, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same comparator sets, including MDM, T2M-GPT, StableMoFusion, MARDM, and MoMask on SnapMoGen. Disabling caption augmentation is an internal ablation rather than an added comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 adds an augmentation-disabled control and a diagnostic using 32 prompts, 10 decoding iterations, and scales containing 10/20/40/80 tokens. The reorganized tables also revise reported settings: the CLIP ablation now falls under two VQ layers rather than v1's four-layer base, and Table 4 specifies 284 latent dimensions instead of 384, conflicting with the retained implementation description. Whether these setting revisions reflect reruns is unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds two focused analyses: the effect of disabling caption augmentation in Table 5(A), and which token scales complete earlier during inference in Figure 5. Existing reconstruction, architecture, text-encoder, and overfitting analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state 20 experimental repetitions and report 95% confidence intervals for the main benchmark results. No additional seed information, statistical tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 retain their numerical results. New Table 5(A) reports FID 17.98 and CLIP score 0.656 without caption augmentation, versus 15.56 and 0.684 for the augmented baseline. New Figure 5 shows earlier completion of coarse-scale tokens during decoding.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7) and the evaluation-model objective in Appendix B.2 remain mathematically unchanged. The new decoding analysis adds empirical observations without a new formal definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning expressive motion annotations, efficient MoMask++ generation, benchmark performance, and LLM-assisted handling of casual prompts.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly interprets coarse-scale-first token completion as an emergent global-to-local generation strategy and attributes it to attention prioritizing semantic importance. The dataset and model limitations in Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the exact token-scale configuration and decoding budget for the new diagnostic and revises ablation hyperparameter descriptions, including the inconsistent latent-dimension specification. Existing hardware, training recipes, evaluator details, prompt templates, and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The same 39 references and the substantive research positioning in Section 2 are retained. Bibliographic formatting and pagination changes do not alter the cited works.

P1.justification: Section 5.2 receives localized rewriting to separate VQ and transformer analyses and explain token-completion behavior. An author contact changes and an empty NeurIPS Paper Checklist heading is added; the broader narrative and appendix structure remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the conditioning panels in Figure 2, splits the combined ablation table into Tables 4–5 with descriptive row labels, and adds the decoding-progress plot. The existing validation-loss plot is enlarged and relocated as Figure 6; appendix figures and prompt tables retain their content under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The new augmentation ablation provides direct evidence for the benefit of augmented captions, while the decoding analysis and clearer ablation tables improve understanding. These are limited gains because the main benchmark evidence remains unchanged. The inconsistent latent dimension in Table 4 and unexplained change in the CLIP ablation's VQ setting temper the improvement by reducing reproducibility clarity.
